rules.title: California tenant screening fee cap and screening fee rules
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a tenant screening fee only up to the annually adjusted state maximum ($68.96 for 2026), and only to cover actual costs such as a consumer credit report and processing. The landlord must give the applicant a copy of the credit report within 7 days of receiving it, a receipt itemizing out-of-pocket costs and time spent, and a refund of any unused portion. The landlord must accept a reusable screening report the tenant provides. No fee may be charged if no unit is actually available. The fee must be returned to applicants who are not selected, unless the landlord reviews applications in order received, rents to the first qualified applicant, and charges no fee to applicants not considered.
rules.interaction: Restated on a Berkeley Rent Board page. Berkeley Mun. Code § 13.78.010 requires owners to disclose this state fee cap.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee rights statement disclosure
rules.requirement: An owner or agent who charges an applicant a fee for a credit report or application processing must give a clear and conspicuous Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and a statement of the maximum fee cap under Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b). The disclosure must appear in the rental application or in a separate disclosure before the fee is received.
rules.key_value: Pre-fee disclosure of screening fee rights and state maximum fee cap required
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in Berkeley where the owner charges a screening/application fee
rules.interaction: Implements disclosure of the state fee cap in Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(b). Under BMC 13.78.018, Chapter 13.78 applies to all rental agreements regardless of contrary lease language.

rules.title: Berkeley ban on non-refundable fees for existing tenancies
rules.requirement: Owners and agents may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy in whole or in part. This includes fees tied to a roommate leaving and fees for requests to add or replace a roommate in an existing household. Lease provisions that violate Chapter 13.78 are unenforceable.
rules.key_value: No non-refundable renewal or roommate-change fees for existing tenants
rules.interaction: Under BMC 13.78.018, applies to all residential rental agreements regardless of contrary contractual language.
rules.quoted_span: cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
rules.penalty: Lease provisions violating Chapter 13.78 are unenforceable (BMC 13.78.018)
